steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Combine flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl. Beat softened butter, shortening, sugar, brown sugar, and vanilla in another bowl until creamy. Beat in egg, then gradually add flour mixture and mix well. Stir in chocolate chips.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet until edges are starting to turn golden brown, about 8 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Soft Chocolate Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These easy soft chocolate chip cookies with chocolate chips in every bite are ready to share in no time. Sure to be a hit!
raw_recipe.name: Easy Soft Chocolate Chip Cookies

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Combine flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl. Beat softened butter, shortening, sugar, brown sugar, and vanilla in another bowl until creamy. Beat in egg, then gradually add flour mixture and mix well. Stir in chocolate chips.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet until edges are starting to turn golden brown, about 8 to 10 minutes.

review.reviewBody: The recipe is basically the same as the Toll House recipe with half butter and half shortening. For those that don't know - shortening allows these cookies to remain moist and chewy longer and not get too hard if baked a bit too long (like all-butter ones). Good recipe - it's what I've started to do with most cookie recipes calling for all butter, if I wanted them to come out a bit chewier.

These are quite possibly the best chocolate chip cookies I've ever made! The shortening helps the cookie stay soft and not flatten out. The butter gives it great flavor. I love that it's such a basic and simple recipe. I used unsalted butter and increased the salt to 3/4 tsp. (I like my cookies a little saltier - makes them more addictive!). I chilled the dough before baking and scooped the cookies into high mounds to help them not flatten out. I also used a full 2 cups chocolate chips, saving the extra 1/2 cup chips to press on top of the cookies right after they came out of the oven. These are definitely soft and stay soft. I just ate one from the batch I made yesterday and yep, still soft and delicious! I'm so excited to have found my go-to recipe for chocolate chip cookies!

Excellent. Take them out of the oven when they have sunk down to flat, but haven't browned all over yet. For my oven it's around 9 minutes. Then let them sit and finish setting up on the sheet pan. Don't move them until they are cool.
Excellent. Used all butter instead of part shortening, but reduced total butter by 1 Tablespoon. Cookies had some thickness. They disappeared but we want more.

I loved these! Best chocolate chip recipe I've made in a long time! I doubled the recipe and it was perfect. 

I let my kitchenaid stand mixer beat the outta the sugars, butter+shortening, vanilla before I added the eggs then dry ingredients. The perfect bake time for my oven was exactly 10 minutes. They turned golden as they cooled. I'm grateful for this recipe!
Great recipe! I made mini cookies using a small cookie scoop and cutting it in half. I used mini chocolate chips and baked for 9 minutes. They turned out great!

My family can't wait til I makes these cookies!! Simply perfect, I love them. I always double the recipe and I have had no problems with them coming out hard. I sub the regular sugar for brown sugar and there is no difference. My kids have gotten creative and besides chocolate chips we've used peanut butter chips and plain m & m's. It's great that this recipe is fast and easy. Doe is very soft when first made but don't be alarmed, I sometimes put it in the fridge for a few hrs prior to baking. I never thought making cookies on my own could turn out to be this good!
I added chopped pecans.... And keep dough in the refrigerator... To make a few at a time....

I have made this recipe multiple times and followed the recipe as wrote. Every time they have turned out to be the best cookies. I decided to try to make them gluten-free using krusteaze gluten-free all purpose flour. This flour is my favorite for baking since we have dietary restrictions for several members of my household. They turned out perfect!!!!!

I loved these! Added a little more butter, a bit more baking soda, and mixed in almond flavoring with the vanilla (probably doubling the flavoring amount). Made heaping ice-cream-scoop rounds (pressing them down a little) and baked at 350 for 10-12 minutes. The result: chewy delicious, melt-in-your-mouth monster cookies! Yes!

They turned out awesome. I did double the recipe but I reduced the flour by a 1/2 cup to keep them soft. I made a couple of double batches in which I substituted the chocolate chips for Carob chips and added Craisins which I re-hydrated a little bit in some water and drained them before adding them in. I also kept the temp at 350 degrees and upped the time to 12 mins, which will vary depending on the size of your cookie.

I did t have shortening or brown sugar so I used the equivalent in butter and the equivalent of white sugar, I also added 2 extra eggs. They came out great, and were not as sweet as regular chocolate chip cookies which I loved since I'm not too into sweets.
I didn't have shortening so I doubled the butter. I used BOTH milk chocolate AND white chocolate chips. Still amazingly delicious. Will definitely make many more times.

I absolutely loved these cookies, and so did my family! I didn't have any vanilla extract, but maple syrup worked just fine and added an autumnal flavour that reminded me of my favourite season. 10/10 would bake again!

I'm 16 and made these with my grandma today to leave out for Santa clause. We haven't tried them yet but they look pretty good. We made 20 of them and accidentally made them to big they cooked together we are going to cut them and try them tho
I've tried a lot of recipes for soft chocolate chip cookies, this recipe wins the gold medal!!!

Easy enough to follow, you can make them crunchy or soft and it still tastes good, I brought a double batch of this to work and everyone loved them. It made a bunch of cookies, more than enough for my work event that had 40 people, keeping in mind not everyone ate them, but some ate more than one. I made them a bit small too. Reminder for all cookies: if you save them in an air tight container, and want them to stay soft, add in a piece or two of bread. The bread will collect all of the stale-ness and the cookies will stay soft. I didn't measure chocolate chips. Followed recipe to a T otherwise. Used plant based crisco shortening
Absolutely delicious. Next time I will add butterfinger chips also :)
this was a great recipe! it was so easy to follow and super fun to make for something that tastes amazing I recommend for people that are beginning baking.,
